April, 1992       Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 C. G. Attwaters......03    04

 Malcolm Wright.......09    10

 Keith Pirie..........14    16

 Alan D. Cox..........18    29

 Brian Cavers.........38     -

 Gerhard Behr.........40    43

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: C.G. Attwaters, NORFOLK

I have just bought a SAM COUPE
with which I am well chuffed. I
also have a Spectrum 48+ and
being a trifle fed up wth tape I
want to transfer the programs to
the SAM. I have tried using the
Emulator on the SAMdisk but have
had no success. I read in a
letter on one of your newsdisks
that some software called
'Specmaker' was a very good buy
and would do the trick.

If you know who sells it, please
let me know, or if you sell it
then please send me an order
form and let me know the price.
Hoping you can help.

                  C.G. Attwaters

Brian Cavers to C.G. Attwaters

Apart from the SAMCO Spectrum
emulator there are several much
more advanced Spectrum emulators
all requiring the user to have a
real Spectrum from which the ROM
can be transferred via tape to
give a greater imitation of a
real Spectrum.

First is our EMUTILITY in OUTLET
34. This provides a menu.A press
of a key and the SAM resets as a
Spectrum. You can then load and
run the majority of Spectrum
programs and save them to SAM
disc. There are extra features
like a RAM SAVE to store a game
position and screen print to
help create game maps.

Game positions can also be saved
to SAM disc to continue the game
another time but the RAM SAVE is
for quickly recovering after a
life has been lost.

Although utility programs will
run under EMUTILITY, there is no
provision to save and load data
to SAM disc or print using the
SAM printer port although it
would be easy for a BASIC prog-
rammer to adapt to say,save/load
and print Tasword 2 files.

EMUTILITY was really designed
for games-playing and does it
well. It is also the cheapest of
all the emulators being just one
item of dozens for the price of
OUTLET (probably works out at
about 20p!)

Another emulator is by LERM.This
is SAMTAPE and the later version
has more features and better
ability to get Spectrum programs
interacting with the disc drive
and printing. It costs `11.99
from LERM,11 Beaconsfield Close,
Whitley Bay, NE25 9UW (add `1 to
Europe, `2 rest of world).

Next is SPECMAKER from SD SOFT-
WARE, 70 Rainhall Road, Barnold-
swick, Lancashire, BB8 6AB. This
works slightly differently in
that a RAMDISK is set up so you
can save from Spectrum mode on
this "pseudo-disc drive in SAM
memory". It's fast, you can use
a printer and you can save the
files on the real SAM disc.
SPECMAKER is `12.95 + 50p post
U.K. (`1.20 elsewhere).

SC SPECLONE is the cheapest as a
stand-alone program. It is only
`1.50 from Steve's Software, 7
Narrow Close, Histon, Cambridge,
CB4 4XX.You can use a printer in
Spectrum utility programs.

The MESSENGER is a gadget that
connects SAM to a Spectrum and
is mainly for games-playing. You
load a game in the Spectrum,load
a special program in the SAM,
press a button and the game is
syphoned rapidly down a cable to
the SAM along with a copy of the
whole of Spectrum memory includ-
ing the ROM! It eliminates any
problems with tape-loading. THE
MESSENGER is `39.99 from SAMCo,
Lakeside, Phoenix Way, Swansea
Enterprise Park,Swansea,SA7 9EH.

Those are the main commercial
Spectrum emulators.SPECMAKER has
been more fully reviewed in
OUTLET 48. Take your pick!

                       - Brian

From Malcolm Wright, CO DURHAM



Dear B.C.,

Do you, or perhaps some of your
OUTLET readers, know of a decent
comms package for the SAM? Some-
thing similar to ACCESS on the
AMIGA would be perfect for what
I intend to do next. As is, the
comms prog that comes with the
SAM interface is DIRE!

          Bye for now!,

         Malcolm Wright

Brian Gaff to Malcolm Wright

Hi, Brian sent your letter to
me, as we were going to release
a scrolling terminal for SAM
last year, but shelved it for a
number of reasons.

Firstly, we have three SAMs, and
not one of them gave decent,
repeatable results through the
RS232, even with a debugged
driver! This turned out to be a
hardware problem caused - we
think - by noise on the power
supply, screwing up the buffer
in the UART chip.

The problem for us is that any
software we release will not
perform the same on everyone's
machines.

I foresaw myself on the phone
most of the day telling users it
was their machines and not our
software that was at fault!

The second problem is the modem.
If you want to dial up services,
you need at least 2400 baud
these days in order to get your
data through before BT end up
with your life savings! Now
until these modems come down to
`70 or so, I cannot forsee great
sales for use on SAM,personally.

Incidentally, you cannot really
go faster than this on SAM, as
the mode 3 screen scrolls too
slowly to be able to get it done
within the time it takes for the
3-character buffer in the comms
interface to fill and overflow.

Even at 2400 baud, special print
routines have to be used to keep
up. Ansi Colour is definitely
out!

A final problem is the handshake
lines on the interface are not
quite right but this can be cop-
ed with by altering the cable.

Now, if you have Pro-Dos, there
is a way to see these problems
quite cheaply. If you buy the PD
Comms disc from FDOS PD, and you
can beg, borrow or whatever, a
modem with Hayes compatability,
you can try ZMP. Assuming your
Comms I/F is not too bad, you
will be able to transfer data at
2400 baud with Zmodem. However,
the screen gets into a terrible
mess on scrolling text!

By the way, Viewdata also gives
us the time problem. In order to
be able to get an accurate
colour resolution, Mode 4 must
be used and this is quite slow.
This brings back the small
buffer problem again. It is
possible though.

                     BG

From: Keith Pirie, ABERDEEN

Dear Cavers boys,

Thanks for Disk 54. Up to the
usual high standard but,Oh Dear!
One minor problem. I always look
forward to viewing the SCREEN$
files. Imagine my surprise when
I view "Fame" in that Issue and
I recognise it as one of the
files currently available on the
"People and Places 1" clip art
collection offered by my comp-
any: Teachers Pet.

Mr. Clayton ordered the collect-
ion in November 1990 and it was
supplied to him on microdrive at
a reduced cost, as I honoured
misprinted information in an
advert to which he responded.

I have no objections to the
SCREEN$ being used in purchasers
programs or newsletters etc.
(after all that is what they are
designed for) but I do object to
customer's presenting them as
their own work and (perhaps)
receiving payment for same.

I know you make payments for
contributions you use and I am
unsure what you may wish to do
about recovering any outlay you
may have made. It is impossible
for you to know which contrib-
utions are genuinely the work of
the submitters. The responsibil-
ity lies with them to be honest.
It is unfortunate that you are
occasionally let down by some.
All the best with future issues.
                     Keith Pirie

Brian Cavers to Keith Pirie


Thanks, Keith.

This is an important point and I
thought it should be published.

I am certain that Chris Clayton
would have sent the screen to us
in all innocence believing it to
be public domain as there are so
many public domain clip art
screens around now. When I get
public domain programs or art
from third parties (i.e., not
orginal to the sender) I do not
usually make any payment and I
am sure, none was expected. This
was the case in the present
situation.

It is worth noting that the clip
art, instead of being marked:-
"by...", was marked, in the
Spectrum version:"SENT IN by..."
and in the SAM version as:-
"FROM..."(this slight change was
probably because I just grabbed
the BASIC from a previous SAM
clip art program instead of
converting the Spectrum BASIC
again). There was no intent to
claim that it was Chris's own
work nor did he represent it to
me as his own work at any time.

I am sorry this has happened and
the lesson is that readers must
be alert that they do not
contribute anything to OUTLET
unless it is their own work or
they know it to be in the public
domain (FREEWARE).      - Brian

From: Alan Cox, DYFED

Do you have a 'Contributors
Guide'you could send me, please?
Various questions come to mind:-
do you expect authors to produce
the opening screen and to
include the various 'extra'
lines to meld the contribution
into OUTLET as a whole? Clearly
you are more than capable of
doing this yourself but I would
be happy to have a go if this is
what you prefer - it would
obviously save your time.

One thing a 'Contributors Guide'
could mention is the need to
remember to comment on whether
the contribution is PD,
copyright or what. I forgot, but
if not too late, 'TILER' is PD.

This reminds me of another
point regarding 'TILER' (OUTLET
55).I'd be very interested to
know whether any of your readers
can dream up a better algorithm.

I was pleased to see Mr.
Ottery's letter giving a full
reference to the edition of SAM
Supplement dealing with transfer
of files between SAM and PCs. I
have written to Brian(?) Mumford
requesting a copy.

In Susan Harvey's letter, and
your response, there is mention
of disk-head cleaners. Maplin
sell these:- for the 3.5" drive
the cost is `2.95 plus their
standard handling charge per
order of `1.00. The article
reference is YT08J.

The address: Maplin Electronics,
PO Box 3,Rayleigh,Essex SS6 8LR.

They also do cleaners for 3" and
5.25" drives.

I know it is not the intenton of
OUTDEX to give selective outputs
but to 'dump' the whole lot.
However, it seems to me it ought
to be possible, say, to give
only those items starting with
the letter G in the Title Search
output.

If you think it is feasible -
and you know how OUTDEX works,
whereas I haven't yet had a go -
I may put it on my project list
and, of course,I would let you
have a copy if I get anywhere.

I take your point about SAMCo's
Newsdisk competing with existing
publications (using this word
broadly). The initial announce-
ment said that they did not want
to duplicate existing things,
but the plans in the first
edition of the Newsdisk appear
to contradict this.

I am sure many people will have
told you the solution to your
'FORMAT wthout Verify' problem
by now, but for the record the
MASTERBASIC manual refers to
DVAR extensions - I am not sure
whether you also need MASTERDOS
- and in particular to DVAR 153
- FVFG which can be POKEd with
an on-zero value to avoid the
verify stage.

I was intrigued by this problem
when you mentioned it in OUTLET
No.54. I thought I would see if
I could illuminate the problem,
even if I could not solve it.

I spent a little unnecessary
time coming to grips with the 3
(at least) different meanings of
verify - i.e. there seems to be
low-level checking in the disk
control chip itself using CRCs,
then there is the 'verify disk'
after FORMAT and finally there
is the BASIC VERIFY command for
a file. Clearly these are all
inter-related, but I do not
think they are all the same
thing.

I am open to correction on this.

It seemed to me that FORMAT had
to lead directly to action in
the disk control chip, since
until the tracks are laid down
and organised the DOS cannot
directly talk to the disk. So I
decided to look at SAMDOS and
see where it addressed the chip
via ports 224 and 240. I soon
ran into a problem, and this is
the real point of raising the
matter in this letter...

The Technical Manual says that
SAM uses the VL-1772-02 disk
controller chip, and there is a
photocopy of the tech spec for
this chip in the annex to the
manual. Unfortunately, the
photocopy says that the chip is
for controlling a 5.25 inch
floppy disk drive.

It refers to the 'physical index
hole', which I think used to be
called 'hard-sectoring'. I know
the phrase, but I think examples
were before my micro-computer
days. It only appears to commun-
icate with the CPU via address
lines A0 and A1, whereas the
Technical Manual refers to A0,
A1, and A2. Have I misunderstood
this, or is it an MGT deliberate
mistake, giving a reference to
the wrong chip? Incidentally, I
think I was getting near to
solving your problem, since I
suspect that only FORMAT and
'disk verify' use track read and
write, rather than sector read
and write, so once I had found
the right part of the DOS a
simple poke of RET would
probably do what you wanted.

In the process of hacking around
the DOS, I came across a refer-
ence to SNOS, which I assume is
the SAM Network Operating
System. Have I missed something,
or is this still to be produced
(and do you know whether it will
then communicate with the net-
work sockets on the Disciple?)

In your review of the COMET
Assembler,you commented adverse-
ly on the fact that you were
required to tell the assembler
the start address and length of
an assembled file before it
could be SAVEd, although, of
course, it already knew. You
then went on to say that you had
hacked into the program and got
over this.

As I am sure you are aware, both
SC_Assembler and LERM's assembl-
er have the same problem. (daft,
to my mind) and I wondered if
you knew of POKEs for either or
both of them to overcome this.

I find both of these programs
very user-unfriendly, albeit in
different ways. The lack of
on-screen menus seems to me the
major snag, especially for those
like me who only use machine
code on and off, and therefore
can easily forget command
abbreviations and structures.

Do you know why LERM only part-
FORMAT their disk? It upsets
Dave Tonk's BITCOPY, which I
tend to use these days to make
back-up copies.

I did try to speed this up with
machine code to replace the use
of READ AT and WRITE AT, but
came to the conclusion that
these BASIC commands are pretty
close to the speed I could get
using hook codes. Incidentally,
you recently mentioned QUICKCOPY
- is this a Spectrum program, or
have I missed it?

Regarding my earlier comments on
the SAM Newsdisk (Outletters
Issues 53 and 54).I am so rarely
in error (and I am so modest
with it!) I can afford to admit
to being wrong occasionally.

I had the chance to look at the
first issue and now believe that
it could be useful to me, so I

have sent a subscription. I have
to say that my erroneous initial
view of the Newsdisk was strong-
ly influenced by its description
in the last SAMCo newsletter.

        All best wishes,

           Alan D. Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

No, we have no "guide to contr-
ibutors" as such. We accept pro-
grams in any form but it does
help enormously if they do not
use lines 1 to 9 (where our
header is inserted - but not
crucial) and (more importantly)
lines 8800 to 9999 where our
OUTLET link BASIC and intro page
will be merged.Most programs can
be renumbered but they are very
difficult if they use calculated
GO TO's or GO SUB's or put the
GO TO or GO SUB in a VAL state-
ment to save memory. Attempts to
reduce memory however, are most
welcome.You can also extract our
OUTLET BASIC and use in your own
program - even using TEXAT to do
a nice header!

Another helpful thing would be
to load any code at line 9000 -
not near the top of the listing
so it keeps reloading every time
you run the program (annoying
when testing). It is also handy
to use the same lines each time
when editing.

However,I must stress, nobody is
EXPECTED or asked to do any of
this - it might just make things
easier for me though!

Thanks for the drive cleaner
information.

The FORMAT-without-VERIFY info
is also most welcome. I did some
tests with the following results
(timed by stopwatch)...

  All timings using MASTERBASIC
 with MASTERDOS and a disc full
     of files such as OUTLET
 WHICH WAS ORIGINALLY FORMATTED
BY AND COPIED TO USING MASTERDOS
 ------------------------------

 Normal FORMAT
 with verify
 plus BACKUP............3m 19s

 FORMAT (no verify)
 plus BACKUP............2m 43s

 FORMAT "D1:" TO "D2:"..2m 58s

The SAMDOS FORMAT D1 TO D2 gave
the same figure as MASTERDOS.You
can see why I have been using
FORMAT D1 TO D2 rather than the
normal FORMAT and BACKUP! Now I
may switch to BACKUP.

Incidentally, if anyone was won-
dering, we duplicate the master
to first copy then the first
copy to the second and so on so
each copy automatically verifies
itself when copying - saving the
need for the normal verify. We
also re-introduce the master in
the chain every 50 or 100 discs
in case an error should start
getting copied and testload one
at the same time.

It should be possible to alter
OUTDEX to print selected names.
The title order print routine
starts at line 300 where line
800 (the start of the data) is
RESTORED.If this RESTORE command
were altered to start at your
chosen initial it should work...

The algorithm for finding the
line number of any program name
in OUTDEX is found by...



  (CODE A$*26+CODE A$(2))*13 +

  INT(CODE A$(3)/2) - 22047


                  ...where A$ is
the program name. To find the
start of a particular initial
letter, for example "G" you need
to add "AA" so A$ should then be
"GAA". You will also need a test
in the print loop to detect when
a name beginning with a letter
greater than "G"(in the example)
to end the listing. Good luck!.

You referred to having found the
text "SNOS" in the DOS.Like you,
I am pretty certain this stands
for SAM Network Operating System
but it was never set up. The
manual makes reference to net-
working but then skillfully (?)
goes on to tell you how to OPEN
a stream to a printer and avoids
telling you how to open a stream
to a network! (User Guide, pp.
118-119). I tried every letter
of the alphabet from OPEN #5;"A"
to"Z"with no flicker of interest
by SAM! My guess is the manual
was rushed out in a hurry before
SAM was complete. MGT were desp-
erate to provide a DOS - any DOS
- for users with DOSless drives!
So, networking was pushed under
the carpet (although it is still
possible in the hardware).

LERM only part-FORMAT their disc
to save time in duplicating.This
is only of benefit on discs that
are only partially full and
would make no difference to an
OUTLET disc which is usually
crammed pretty full! Switch to
FORMAT and COPY "D1:*" to "D2:*"
if you've two drives or, indeed,
use BACKUP! "QUICKCOP" is our
Spectrum with Disciple/+D sector
copier - although it does copy
SAM discs - and is used in the
duplication of SAM OUTLETs! It
is nowhere near as fast as the
SAM copy options though.

It IS strange how SAM assemblers
expect you to save the object
code manually or calculate and
re-enter the start and length
when the program already knows!

I thought I had hacked and done
an auto-save in at least one of
the assemblers you mention but I
can't now find anything on it.
My Lerm disc seems to be mis-
placed and I can't load my 512K
version of SC_Assembler because
my 512K SAM is long, long, long
gone away for repair!

However,a clever person like you
should be able to work it out if
I point you in the right direct-
ion. First,enter a short program
in the assembler editor and
assemble it. Try to give it an
odd length - say 7 bytes.Exit to
BASIC and search using INSTR for
a variable in the code being 7
and 0 for the length and the
equivalent two bytes for the
start (ORG) address.

You may find more than one addr-
ess so repeat using a different
ORG address and length (remember
to re-assemble) until you find
the ones that change in accord-
ance with your code. It is poss-
ible the ORG address may not be
stored as a variable so you may
need to search the text file for
the word ORG(or possibly a token
representing it. Try a string
search for say "ORG 32768" or
whatever.

Then you set up a bit of BASIC
to read these DPEEKS (if ORG in
the text has to be found you
need a short search routine to
find it each time) and input
your filename.Send in your rout-
ine if successful (and state if
256K or 512K).       - Brian

Brian Cavers to Anybody but esp-
ecially Alan Cox & Stuart Burton

Well, I finally got the reset
crash when scrolling up in the
BASIC editor! I feel so pleased
with myself! It happened in LIST
FORMAT 2 mode which I rarely use
(but I'd be interested if you do
use this mode usually).

In LIST FORMAT 2 mode the FOR
NEXT loops are indented. I sudd-
enly noticed the FORs were - but
not the NEXTs! I rubbed my eyes
and scrolled up to see if it was
just a printing glitch. Suddenly
- it was there! The Aurora
Boriwotsit! The SAM RESET screen
colour bars appeared BEHIND the
top of the listing for a few
seconds - then -  a full RESET!

I have not been able to repro-
duce this yet so clearly there
are other factors. In fact, it
may be that the LIST FORMAT 2
theory is just a red herring.The
crash may have just happened at
that time by chance!

My latest problem is in OUTWRITE
BASIC which has just passed the
49152 page boundary and locks up
if I use CLEAR or RUN! By delet-
ing some lines it's O.K. again
but so far, my wheeze of ADDING
dummy lines hasn't cleared it!
I've got a few more tricks up my
sleeve so I hope I can solve it
rather than have to try to
compress the BASIC under 49152!
Oh Sam, Sam! Why do you hate me
so! What did I ever do to you?
                        - Brian

From: Dr.Gerhard Behr, LANCS.


Dear Ron,

You say in your reply to Grant
Dixon (Add-Enders 4, page 17
March 92) that you have broken
into Omnicalc 2's BASIC. I have
been trying to transfer Omnicalc
to SAM for 2 years now, with
Specmaker without success. After
getting Omnicalc on the screen,
there is no way of saving it to
SAM disk. I have tried your line
100, but it makes no difference.

I have the original Spectrum 48K
microdrive version, which saves
automatically to microdrive if
Interface 1 is on the Spectrum.

But, of course, it is not on the
Specmaker-SAM. One can save the
DATA but not the program. It is
strange that they protect the
program so well and allow you to
make as many copies to micro-
drive as you like!

'Omnicalc' 2 is still the best
spreadsheet I know. I have tried
'Perf-Calc' with the new PRODOS,
but it does not do graphics and
one can't use a formula in a
cell using its own cell name. If
I enter an interim dividend in
say g2 and then want to add the
final dividend and enter =g2 +
123, it will add 123 twice and
alter the value in g2 again
every time g2 is mentioned in
another formula.

One can, of course,avoid this by
using the actual value in the
cell instead of the cell name,
but there is no difficulty like
this with 'Omnicalc'. I was,
therefore, very excited, when I
saw that you had been able to
open the program to get back in-
to BASIC and hope you can help.

        Yours sincerely,

          Gerhard Behr

Brian Cavers to Gerhard Behr

I've not tried it but I see no
reason why Omnicalc cannot be
loaded in EMUTILITY (OUTLET 34)
from tape then put on SAM disc.
If data is saved as code,EMUTIL-
ITY BASIC might be adapted to
save it but it is easy just to
resave the whole program includ-
ing data. The print option won't
work though. You may get on
better with LERM's SAMTAPE (see
reply to C.G. Attwaters). This
diverts the Spectrum print
routines to the SAM's. I think
SC SPECLONE does the same. My
advice would be wait a month or
so when we hope to announce an
exciting new spreadsheet for the
SAM - the best yet!
                         - Brian.

From: C.G. Attwaters, NORFOLK

I have just bought a SAM COUPE with which I am well chuffed. I also have a Spectrum 48+ and being a trifle fed up wth tape I want to transfer the programs to the SAM. I have tried using the Emulator on the SAMdisk but have had no success. I read in a letter on one of your newsdisks that some software called 'Specmaker' was a very good buy and would do the trick.

If you know who sells it, please let me know, or if you sell it then please send me an order form and let me know the price. Hoping you can help.

C.G. Attwaters

Brian Cavers to C.G. Attwaters

Apart from the SAMCO Spectrum emulator there are several much more advanced Spectrum emulators all requiring the user to have a real Spectrum from which the ROM can be transferred via tape to give a greater imitation of a real Spectrum.

First is our EMUTILITY in OUTLET 34. This provides a menu.A press of a key and the SAM resets as a Spectrum. You can then load and run the majority of Spectrum programs and save them to SAM disc. There are extra features like a RAM SAVE to store a game position and screen print to help create game maps.

Game positions can also be saved to SAM disc to continue the game another time but the RAM SAVE is for quickly recovering after a life has been lost.

EMUTILITY was really designed for games-playing and does it well. It is also the cheapest of all the emulators being just one item of dozens for the price of OUTLET (probably works out at about 20p!)

### От: Dr. Gerhard Behr, LANCS.

Дорогой Ron,

В своем ответе Grant Dixon (Add-Enders 4, страница 17, март 92) вы говорите, что взломали BASIC в Omnicalc 2. Я пытаюсь перенести Omnicalc на SAM уже 2 года с помощью Specmaker, но безуспешно. После того как Omnicalc появляется на экране, нет никакой возможности сохранить его на диск SAM. Я пробовал вашу строку 100, но это ничего не меняет.

У меня есть оригинальная microdrive-версия для Spectrum 48K, которая автоматически сохраняет на microdrive, если на Spectrum подключен Interface 1.

Но, разумеется, его нет на Specmaker-SAM. Можно сохранить DATA, но не саму программу. Странно, что они так хорошо защитили программу, но при этом позволяют делать сколько угодно копий на microdrive!

'Omnicalc' 2 — по-прежнему лучшая электронная таблица из всех, что я знаю. Я пробовал 'Perf-Calc' с новой PRODOS, но она не поддерживает графику, и там нельзя использовать формулу в ячейке с указанием имени этой же ячейки. Если я ввожу промежуточный дивиденд, скажем, в g2, а затем хочу добавить окончательный дивиденд и ввожу =g2 + 123, она прибавит 123 дважды и будет снова изменять значение в g2 каждый раз, когда g2 упоминается в другой формуле.

Конечно, этого можно избежать, используя фактическое значение в ячейке вместо имени ячейки, но с 'Omnicalc' таких проблем не возникает. Поэтому я был очень взволнован, увидев, что вам удалось вскрыть программу и вернуться в BASIC, и надеюсь, вы сможете помочь.

Искренне ваш,  
Gerhard Behr
